chunks: And those who believe say: 'Why is not a Surah revealed?' But when a categorical Surah is revealed that mentions war, you see those in whose hearts is disease looking at you with the glance of one swooning in death. So better for them.

key_terms.الْمَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ: One who has fainted or swooned
key_terms.قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ: Disease in their hearts (a metaphor for hypocrisy and doubt)
key_terms.مُحْكَمَةٌ: Categorical or clear (referring to a Surah with specific rulings)

ai.seo_question: What was the reaction of the hypocrites when the Surah of fighting was revealed?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological state of the hypocrites (al-maraḍ al-qalbī) who, despite outwardly professing faith, were paralyzed by fear when the command for active combat was revealed, contrasting with the steadfastness of the true believers. The imagery of 'gazing like the dying' underscores their spiritual death and confusion in the face of divine authority. This event is often cited to illustrate the transition from the Meccan period of patience to the Medinan era of political and military engagement.
